what: CACI does technology work for the American government: intelligence systems, secure communications, electronic warfare equipment and software modernisation, mostly under long contracts with defence and intelligence agencies.
customers: The Department of Defense, intelligence agencies and federal civilian departments.
money: mission support, intelligence analysis and engineering services
software, secure communications and electronic warfare products
moat: Security clearances and incumbency: thousands of cleared staff already embedded in agency programmes, which a competitor cannot assemble in time to bid credibly.
risks: All revenue depends on federal budgets and the timing of appropriations
$5.4B of debt against $192M of cash after a run of acquisitions
A 5.6% net margin, normal for government services but thin
opportunities: Revenue grew from $6.2B to $9.6B in four years, faster than its peers
Analysts see about 23% upside, with 15 covering the stock
The shift toward its own technology products rather than staff hours raises the margin
watch: Contract awards and the backlog, and whether the technology half keeps outgrowing services.
